quote: We distinguish machinic enslavement and social subjection as two separate concepts
There is enslavement when human beings themselves are
constituent pieces of a machine that they compose among themselves and with other things
under the control and direction of a higher unity
there is subjection when the higher unity constitutes the human being as a subject linked to a now exterior object
The human being is no longer a component of the machine but a worker, a user
One is not enslaved by the technical machine but rather subjected to it
capital acts as the point of subjectification that constitutes all human beings as subjects
cybernetic and informational machines form a third age
the relation between human and machine is based on internal, mutual communication, and no longer on usage or action
a subject of the statement that more or less mistakes itself for a subject of enunciation
In machinic enslavement, there is nothing but transformations and exchanges of information, some of which are mechanical, others human
two simultaneous parts that constantly reinforce and nourish each other
Rather than stages, subjection and enslavement constitute two coexistent poles
This is not to say that the second regime is more human
a generalized "machinic enslavement," such that one may furnish surplus-value without doing any work
